name_reason: Accurate STATUS-CURE worker name following fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>; clears a status byte and heals +10 HP (the cure direction, opposite of the inflict sibling fd2_cast_status_inflict_spell @ 0x22D1B). No Ghidra address residue; 'status_cure' is a semantic descriptor. Reached both via item use-effect dispatch (effects 6/antidote, 7/de-paralyze) and via the 0x14/0x15 spell wrapper, and curing/clearing is its core behavior.
purpose: Status-cure spell/item worker: for each target, if the selected status byte is set, clear it, heal +10 HP, and credit XP; otherwise show a miss.
logic_summary: Plays per-target impact + status-overlay-flicker animations. For iter 0..n_targets-1: target_id = ((uint8*)p_targets)[iter]; target_rc = &runtime_char[target_id]; level_mod = pStatus_flags_block[0] (level byte at offset 0x21), +0x1e if 8 < job_id < 0x19 (intermediate class); read the status byte at raw offset (target_rc + sprite_id). If that byte == 0 -> fd2_show_miss_indicator(target_id). Else heal = fd2_apply_hp_heal_and_award_xp(target_id, 10); fd2_show_damage_number(heal, 0x69 'i', target_id); clear the status byte to 0; pending_xp_credit += level_mod*4 (cure tier is 4x vs 2x for AP/DP/speed buffs). Closes with fd2_composite_battle_frame(0). Verified against decompile + disassembly (0x22B5D loads runtime_char base; 0x22B64 MOVZX [EBX+0x21]=level; 0x22B68 MOVZX [EBX+0x20]=job; 0x22B79-0x22B7F status byte at rc+sprite_id; 0x22B8C PUSH 0xa; 0x22B9E PUSH 0x69; 0x22BA9 MOV byte[ESI],0; 0x22BAC SHL EBP,2 then ADD [0x53ec8]).
signature: void fd2_cast_status_cure_spell(uint32 caster, uint32 spell_id, uint32 n_targets, uint32 p_targets, uint32 sprite_id)

params.name: caster
params.semantics: Caster unit id; forwarded to the impact/overlay animation calls (not used in the per-target cure loop).
params.reason: Accurate, address-free. (Live Ghidra decompile labels params 1-3 generically as param_1/2/3 and mislabels the 4th as caster_idx; the C source already carries the correct names, which is what is judged here.)

params.name: spell_id
params.semantics: Animation/spell id passed to fd2_animate_spell_impact_per_target and fd2_animate_status_effect_overlay_flicker (e.g. 0x14/0x15 from the spell wrapper; 0x14/0x15 from item effects 6/7).

params.name: n_targets
params.semantics: Number of entries in the p_targets byte array; signed loop bound.

params.name: p_targets
params.semantics: Pointer (as uint32) to a byte array of target unit ids; each entry indexes data_fd2_battle_runtime_char_array_ptr. Asm reads *(byte*)(p_targets + iter).
params.reason: Accurate, address-free. (Ghidra's live decompile mislabels this 4th param as caster_idx; the C source name p_targets is correct per usage.)

params.name: sprite_id
params.semantics: Raw runtime_char byte offset selecting which status byte to test/clear. Callers pass 0x25 (poison byte at pStatus_flags_block[4], item effect 6/antidote) and 0x26 (bStatus_sleep_flag, item effect 7/de-paralyze). Asm: status byte = byte ptr [rc_base + sprite_id]; Ghidra renders it via its struct as pSprite_state[sprite_id-2] (pSprite_state at +0x02, so the index resolves to the same +sprite_id byte).
params.reason: Established term shared with the inflict sibling (fd2_cast_status_inflict_spell uses the same sprite_id offset parameter); address-free. The name is slightly generic (it is a struct byte offset, not literally a sprite id), but renaming would churn the whole status-spell family for marginal gain; documented in the comment instead. Keep.

returns.semantics: No return value. Side effects: clears per-target status bytes, applies HP heals, accumulates data_fd2_battle_pending_xp_credit, drives on-screen number/miss indicators and the composite battle frame.

comment_original_issue: The sprite_id example mapping was imprecise: it listed '0x25=poison, 0x26=sleep, 0x27=silence', but 0x27 is never passed by either caller of this function (only the inflict sibling @ 0x22D1B uses 0x27), and the labels did not tie to the actual struct fields or caller paths. Per the Ghidra runtime_char struct, 0x25 = pStatus_flags_block[4] and 0x26 = bStatus_sleep_flag; the two real caller paths are item effect 6/antidote (0x25) and effect 7/de-paralyze (0x26).
notes: 3-source verified (plate + decompile + disassembly) and cross-checked against the Ghidra runtime_char struct layout and both callers (fd2_apply_use_effect_dispatch effects 6/7 pass 0x14/0x25 and 0x15/0x26; fd2_apply_status_effect_with_anim forwards spell 0x14/0x15 from fd2_cast_spell_14_dispatch_aa8). level_mod base = pStatus_flags_block[0] (offset 0x21, the level byte) is consistent across 6 sibling spell workers. Plate left unchanged: it is detailed, consistent with the refined understanding, and explicitly flags the struct-misnaming caveat; only the src parenthetical needed tightening (rule: update plate only when contradictory/stale/blank). No logic changed; comment-only edit. Name + all 5 param names kept (no Stage 2 rename queued).
